transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. I came in because I've been having some trouble lately with my eating. After my late shifts, I'll stop for food on the way back, but then I just... keep going once I get home. I'll eat a full takeout meal, and then move on to chips, sweets, basically whatever is in the apartment. Afterward, I look at the wrappers and I'm honestly shocked by how much I actually ate. It's been really bothering me.
After these episodes of eating a lot, do you do anything to try to counteract it — like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or restricting what you eat the next day?

Yeah, I do. Honestly, since the apartment move settled into a routine, it's been happening most weeks. I'll have at least one of these late-night episodes where I just eat way past what I meant to. And when I realize what I've done, I try to make up for it. Usually, I'll make myself throw up... or I'll just skip breakfast the next morning, or force myself to go on a really long run to try and burn it all off.
During these late-night eating episodes, do you feel like you're unable to stop eating or control how much you're eating while it's happening?

Yeah, that's exactly what it feels like. Once I start on those nights... it's almost like I'm watching myself from the outside. I'll be in my head telling myself to just put the food away, but I can't. My hands just keep opening containers and packages until everything is gone. I just completely lose control of it.

BED diagnosis is supported by the pattern of loss of control during eating episodes and subsequent compensatory behaviors.
